# acquire

Most methods here fetch content with
[fossick](https://github.com/vedicreader/fossick) and file the result
with
[`Vault.add`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/core.html#vault.add).
The `meta` of each document records its source URL and the fetch time. A
document found by `web` also records the query that found it.

### clip

``` python
def clip(
    s:str, n:int=120
)->str:
```

*Collapse the whitespace in a scraped title and cut it to `n`
characters.*

`url` reads one page and converts it to markdown. Many sites answer a
script with a challenge page, called a bot wall, instead of the article.
With `auto=True`, the default, fossick then tries a heavier fetcher,
then a stealthy browser, then your logged-in Chrome.

`crawl` follows links from a start page and files each page it reaches.
It skips a page whose markdown is empty.

`web` runs a web search, reads the top `n` results and files them. It
stores the query in the `meta` of each document. The `dropped` key of
the result lists the results it could not read.

``` python
def url(
    url:str, # page to read
    title:str=None, # defaults to the page's first heading, else its path
    sel:str=None, # CSS selector to narrow the page before conversion
    kind:str='web', # kind the document is filed as
    auto:bool=True, # past a bot wall, escalate plain -> heavy -> stealthy -> logged-in Chrome
    meta:dict=None, # extra meta; the reader's own keys replace any that match

    progress:NoneType=None, # told `progress(1, 1, [url])` once the page is filed
    **kw
)->dict: # forwarded to fossick.fetch (verify=, headers=, heavy=…)
```

*Fetch one URL, convert it to markdown and file it in the vault.*

`grab` does not file a source file on GitHub as a document. It clones
the repository and indexes it with kosha as code.

With `crawl=True`, `grab` calls `crawl` on the target whatever its kind.
With `shelf=`, `grab` files the result on that named shelf. Without it,
`grab` uses the shelf that `KIND_SHELF` names for the kind of the
target.

*File an arXiv paper, with its metadata and full text, as kind `arxiv`

A directory usually holds two kinds of file. `add_dir` files prose, such
as Markdown, notebooks and PDFs, in the vault. `index_code` sends source
code to [kosha](03_code.ipynb), a separate index built for code.
`add_tree` does both, and `grab` calls it for a directory.

If kosha fails, `add_tree` issues a warning and leaves the source files
out. It does not file them as prose. `connect=True` runs `connect` once
at the end. It does not run if `stop` cancelled the ingest or if nothing
was filed.

You can stop a long ingest. `add_tree`, `add_dir` and `add_files` take
two callbacks.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Argument</th>
<th>When it is called</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>stop</code></td>
<td>Before each batch of <code>batch</code> files (50), before each file
in a batch, and before kosha.</td>
</tr>
<tr>

<td>As <code>progress(done, total, batch)</code> after each batch.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

When `stop()` returns True, the files already filed stay in the vault.
The result has `cancelled` set and `unread` lists the files not reached.
No exception is raised. A fetch already under way finishes.

The other methods take `stop` and `progress` too. `grab` accepts both
for any target.

``` python
def add_tree(
    dir:str, # tree to ingest
    types:str='.pdf,.md,.markdown,.txt,.rst,.ipynb,.xml,.tei,.htm,.html,.conllu', # extensions filed into the vault as prose
    code:bool=True, # index source files with kosha, when the tree has any
    kind:str=None, # override the kind for the prose half

    batch:int=50, # files per job when queueing, and per batch filed when `stop` or `progress` is given
    stop:NoneType=None, # asked between batches and before kosha; True stops, and `unread` holds the files not reached
    progress:NoneType=None, # told `progress(done, total, batch)` after each batch of documents
    **kw
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict: # forwarded to add_file
```

*Add the documents in a directory to the vault and its source code to
kosha. With `queue=True`, queue the work instead.*

### Fanning an ingest out

A large tree can take hours. `add_tree(..., queue=True)` puts the work
on the vault’s job queue (see [jobs](11_jobs.ipynb)) instead of doing
it. A crash then costs only the batch in flight.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Job</th>
<th>Count</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Ingest of <code>batch</code> files (50)</td>
<td>One per batch</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Code indexing with kosha</td>
<td>One, when the tree has source files</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>connect</code></td>
<td>One, with <code>connect=True</code>. It waits until every ingest job
has run.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

Nothing runs until something runs the queue, such as `poll` or
`vault.q.drain()`. `jobs(kind='ingest')` shows the jobs that remain.

The vault skips a file it already holds, so running a batch twice does
no harm. A retried batch files only the files it missed. Queueing a
batch that is still waiting adds no second job.

### Harvest: read a page’s API, not its HTML

Many sites, shops in particular, fill a page with data from a JSON API
that the page calls in the background. Reading that API gives clean
records instead of scraped HTML.

`apis(url)` loads the page and captures the JSON calls it makes. It
lists them with the number of records in each.

`harvest(url)` replays one captured call. It runs `apis` first, unless
you pass `capture=` and the
[`Vault`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/core.html#vault)
object holds an earlier `apis` result. `capture=` is the `n` of a call
in that result. Without `capture=`, it picks the call with the most
records. It follows the pagination of the call when `pages` is more
than 1. It files the records as one document of kind `data`, with one
section per record.

`add_records` files a list of dicts you already have, from any API or
export, in the same way.

### Watches

A watch repeats an acquisition on a schedule.
`watch(target, action=..., every='6h')` registers one. `ACTIONS` lists
the actions, and `kind=` is another name for `action`.

<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Action</th>
<th>What each run does</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>url</code></td>
<td>Re-reads a page.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>web</code></td>
<td>Re-runs a web search.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>harvest</code></td>
<td>Re-harvests an API.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>arxiv</code>, <code>youtube</code></td>
<td>Re-reads a paper or a video.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>crawl</code></td>
<td>Re-crawls a site.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>path</code></td>
<td>Calls <code>grab</code> on a path.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>folder</code></td>
<td>Reports changes in a folder.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>remind</code></td>
<td>Writes a reminder note.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

`every` takes an interval such as `'30m'`, `'1d'` or `'1w'`. `cron=`
takes a five-field cron expression instead. Other keyword arguments go
to the action, such as `n=5` for a web search.

The clock is [pobblebonk](https://vedicreader.github.io/pobblebonk/),
which keeps its schedules in the vault file. `poll()` is the tick to
call from cron, a scheduler or an app’s timer. Each call does these
steps in order:

1.  It returns jobs whose worker died to the queue.
2.  It queues a job for every watch that is due.
3.  It runs the queue.
4.  It runs `connect` if any job succeeded and `connect=True`.
5.  It runs `housekeep` if 600 seconds have passed since the last run on
    this connection.

A failed fetch, or one that hit a bot wall, is retried after a growing
delay. After 5 attempts the job is dead. `jobs(state='dead')` lists dead
jobs, and `retry_job` puts one back on the queue. A worker killed in the
middle of a fetch loses its claim on the job, called its lease. The job
itself goes back on the queue.

The next run is counted from when the last run was due. A slow fetch
does not push later runs back. After a gap, such as a laptop asleep for
ten hours under an hourly watch, `catchup` (1 by default) sets how many
missed runs to make up. `missed` counts the rest. `run_watch` fires one
watch now, outside the queue. `pause` disables a watch and keeps it.
`unwatch` deletes it. The documents a watch filed stay in both cases.

A `folder` watch takes a snapshot of the files under a folder, or of
those matching `pattern`. The snapshot holds at most 5000 files. A run
reports the files added, changed or removed since the last snapshot. A
`folder` watch needs `instructions`, the standing brief for whoever
reviews the change. Every report includes the `instructions`. A `remind`
watch writes or updates one note and fetches nothing.

`housekeep` marks a document stale in these cases:

<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Source</th>
<th>Stale when</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Local file</td>
<td>The file was deleted, or changed after it was filed.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Web page</td>
<td>30 days have passed and no watch refreshes it.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Video</td>
<td>90 days have passed and no watch refreshes it.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Data harvest</td>
<td>7 days have passed and no watch refreshes it.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

Where a watch has filed several copies of one source, `housekeep` marks
the older copies superseded. With `prune=True`, the default, it deletes
the documents that are both stale and superseded.

``` python
def watch(
    target:str, # URL, query, arXiv id, path, folder, or the text of a reminder
    action:str='url', # one of ACTIONS: what to do when it fires
    every:str='1d', # interval: '30m', '6h', '1d', '1w', '1M', or seconds
    cron:str=None, # or a five-field cron expression, instead of an interval
    note:str=None, # why you are watching
    start:float=None, # first run time (epoch); an interval watch defaults to now, a cron watch to its next match
    catchup:int=1, # missed intervals to make up after a gap; the rest count as `missed`
    kind:str=None, # alias for action; what the target set calls it
    instructions:str='', # the standing brief a folder watch's reviewer gets, verbatim
    pattern:str='', # globs limiting a folder watch
    **params
)->dict: # forwarded to the action (n=, pages=, sel=, ...)
```

### Images

A photo has no text to search. The vault files what the image file says
about itself: its size, the camera, and when and where it was taken
(from its EXIF data). It also files any caption or labels you add.
`labels=` holds what an image classifier saw. A search for “galah” then
finds a picture of a galah. The pixels stay on disk, and the `path` key
in the `meta` of the document points at them.

``` python
def add_image(
    path:str, # the picture
    title:str=None, # defaults to the filename
    caption:str=None, # a description, if you have one
    labels:NoneType=None, # what a classifier saw
    meta:dict=None, # your keys replace any the file gives
    force:bool=False, # re-ingest a source already present
    **kw
)->dict: # forwarded to `add`
```

*File one picture as `kind="image"`. Its metadata is the searchable
text. The pixels stay on disk.*

`label_images` runs [anya](https://github.com/vedicreader/anya), an
image classifier, over a folder. It files every picture with the labels
it found, with `force=True`, and you can then search the pictures by
what is in them. It raises `ImportError` when anya is not installed.

href="https://github.com/vedicreader/vishalakshi/blob/main/vishalakshi/acquire.py#L685"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
    min_score:float=0.0, # ignore anything less confident
    add:bool=True, # file them in the vault as well as returning them
    **kw
)->fastcore.foundation.L: # forwarded to anya.classify
```

*Classify a folder with anya and file every picture in the vault with
what the model saw.*

``` python
_m,_g = exif_meta(wren_path), exif_meta(galah_path)
_md, _gmd=image_md(_m, 'Superb-fairy-wren.-008', labels=['Superb Fairywren']), image_md(_g, 'galah', labels=['galah'])
assert 'width: 460' in _md
assert 'Superb Fairywren' in _md
```

``` python
_v = Vault(':memory:')
_r = _v.add_image(wren_path, labels=['Superb Fairywren', 'Malurus cyaneus'])
test_eq(_v.stats()['by_kind']['image'], 1)
test_eq(_v.doc(str(wren_path.resolve()))['meta']['labels'][0], 'Superb Fairywren')
assert first(_v.search('Superb Fairywren', kind='image')), 'labels have to be searchable'
test_eq(len(_v.add_images(Path.cwd(), force=True)), 2)
test_eq(len(_v.images()), 2)
# what a later model run adds is merged in, and the text is rebuilt so it is searchable too
_ = _v.tag_image(str(galah_path.resolve()), labels=['Galah'], caption='pink and grey')
test_eq(_v.doc(str(galah_path.resolve()))['meta']['labels'], ['Galah'])
assert first(_v.search('pink and grey', kind='image'))
```

## Try it

``` python
v = Vault(':memory:')
v.add_records([dict(sku='A1', name='Free range eggs', price=4.5),
               dict(sku='B2', name='Oat milk', price=2.1)], 'dairy')
v.search('eggs')[0]['breadcrumb']
```

``` python
import os
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
```

``` python
# fossick's json_records walk; harvest pagination uses the same
_pay = {'data': {'items': [{'a': 1}, {'a': 2}, {'a': 3}]}}
test_eq(len(json_records(_pay)), 3)
test_eq(json_records(_pay, with_key=True)[1], 'items')
test_eq(secs('6h'), 21600); test_eq(secs('1w'), 604800); test_eq(secs(90), 90)
test_eq(secs('30m'), 1800); test_eq(secs('2 days'), 172800); test_eq(secs('45s'), 45)
test_eq(secs('1h30m'), 5400); test_eq(secs('90'), 90)
test_fail(lambda: secs('whenever'), contains='not a duration')
w = v.watch('late chunking', action='web', every='1d', n=3)
test_eq(w['params'], dict(n=3))
test_eq(len(v.watches(due_only=True)), 1)
v.unwatch(w['id'])
test_eq(len(v.watches()), 0)

# a folder watch snapshots what is there and fires only on what moved; `kind` is `action` by another name
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    v = Vault(':memory:', offline=True)
    (Path(d)/'a.py').write_text('a = 1')
    test_fail(lambda: v.watch(d, kind='folder', every='5m'), contains='instructions')
    w = v.watch(Path(d), kind='folder', every='5m', instructions='flag any print()', pattern='*.py')   # a Path target is filed as text
    test_eq((w['kind'], w['action'], w['instructions'], w['pattern']), ('folder', 'folder', 'flag any print()', '*.py'))
    test_eq(list(w['params']['snap']), [str(Path(d)/'a.py')])
    test_eq(v.watches()[0]['kind'], 'folder'); test_eq(v.watches()[0]['pattern'], '*.py')
    test_eq(v.run_watch(v.watches()[0])['status'], 'skipped')                          # nothing moved
    (Path(d)/'b.py').write_text('print(2)'); (Path(d)/'a.py').write_text('a = 2'); os.utime(Path(d)/'a.py', (time.time()+1,)*2)
    (Path(d)/'c.txt').write_text('ignored')
    r = v.run_watch(v.watches()[0])
    test_eq((r['status'], sorted(Path(p).name for p in r['result']['added']), [Path(p).name for p in r['result']['changed']]), ('ok', ['b.py'], ['a.py']))
    test_eq(r['result']['instructions'], 'flag any print()')
    test_eq(v.run_watch(v.watches()[0])['status'], 'skipped')                          # snapshot advanced
    os.utime(Path(d)/'a.py', (time.time()-100,)*2)                                      # an older file checked out is a change too
    test_eq([Path(p).name for p in v.run_watch(v.watches()[0])['result']['changed']], ['a.py'])
    u = v.watch('https://x.test', action='url', every='1d')                             # old spelling still works
    test_eq((u['kind'], u['instructions'], u['pattern']), ('url', '', ''))
    # a row written before the columns existed reads back with defaults
    v.db.q("update watches set instructions=NULL, pattern=NULL where id=?", [u['id']])
    test_eq((v._watch_row(u['id'])['instructions'], v._watch_row(u['id'])['pattern']), ('', ''))
    # `pattern` is a column now, and a harvest still receives it
    _got = {}
    v.harvest = lambda t, **kw: (_got.update(kw), dict(pages=1))[1]
    h = v.watch('https://x.test/shop', action='harvest', every='1d', pattern='*/api/*', pages=2)
    test_eq((h['pattern'], h['params']), ('*/api/*', dict(pages=2)))
    test_eq(v.run_watch(v._watch_row(h['id']))['status'], 'ok')
    test_eq((_got['pattern'], _got['pages']), ('*/api/*', 2))
```
